subject: general
question: The process by which electrical energy can be produced in a coil involves:

options.text: inclusion of commutator in the system
relative motion of the coil and magnet
magnet and coil under stationary positions
presence of galvanometer in the system

solution:
The correct answer is **__Relative motion of the coil and magnet.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The process by which electrical energy can be produced in a coil primarily involves **the principle of electromagnetic induction. **
 
• This involves changing magnetic fields inducing **electromotive force (EMF) in the coil,** as described by **Faraday's Law of Electromagnetic Induction. **
 
• Some methods to induce emf in a coil are:
 
 
• When a magnet is moved towards or away from a coil, or the coil is moved in relation to the magnet, the flux through the coil changes, inducing an EMF.
 
• In generators, coils of wire are rotated within a magnetic field. As the coil rotates, the angle between the magnetic field and the plane of the coil changes, altering the magnetic flux and inducing an EMF.
 
• A changing current in an adjacent coil can alter the magnetic field through the primary coil, thereby inducing an EMF in the secondary coil.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• Lenz's Law states that the direction of the induced EMF (and hence the induced current) will be such that it opposes the change in magnetic flux that caused it.
 
• Magnetic flux is defined by the product of the magnetic field ( B ), the area of the coil ( A ), and the cosine of the angle between the magnetic field and the normal to the surface of the coil.
